subject.title: fix(sessions): guard JSON.parse in manual compact against corrupted lines

question: Should manual transcript compaction preserve the current atomic failure behavior, or should OpenClaw adopt an explicit, observable recovery policy that permits deleting malformed retained events?
rationale: The patch chooses a persistent user-session data-loss policy for an unproven failure mode; source-level mechanical review cannot determine whether silent deletion is an accepted product recovery contract.

options.title: Preserve atomic compaction
options.body: Remove the per-line skip so a parse failure leaves the existing SQLite transcript untouched; investigate or remove the redundant round trip separately.

options.title: Define recovery explicitly
options.body: Keep recovery only with a documented, observable validation/repair contract that proves which event may be discarded and how users can recover it.

recommendation.title: Preserve atomic compaction
recommendation.body: Remove the per-line skip so a parse failure leaves the existing SQLite transcript untouched; investigate or remove the redundant round trip separately.
